chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated from his paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked: 'Does Allah have the power to place the Earth in an egg, without making the Earth smaller or the egg any bigger?' He replied: 'Woe unto you! Verily, Allah cannot be described by means of limits. Who has more power than He who diminishes the Earth and enlarges the egg?'

key_terms.يُقْدِرُ: To have the power/capacity to do something
key_terms.يُلَطِّفُ: To make fine, subtle, or small

ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology define Allah's power regarding physical limitations?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the Shia theological concept of *al-Lutf* (divine subtlety), where God’s power is not merely brute force but involves precise, effortless manipulation of creation. By citing Imam al-Sadiq’s response to a questioner, the text refutes the idea that divine omnipotence requires altering the intrinsic nature of objects (like shrinking the Earth), affirming instead that God can perform miracles without violating the physical integrity of the created entities. This aligns with the Mu'tazili and Shia emphasis on God’s absolute ability to do anything conceivable, distinguishing His power from human limitations.
